chunks: And do not marry idolatrous women until they believe. And a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress, even though she might please you. And do not marry your daughters to idolaters until they believe. And a believing slave man is better than an idolater, even though he might please you. Those invite to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and to forgiveness by His permission. And He makes clear His verses to the people that they might remember.
ai.seo_question: Why are Muslims prohibited from marrying polytheists according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the primacy of faith (Iman) over social status or beauty in marital selection, often linked with the concept of 'Wilayah' where spiritual alignment ensures harmony. The prohibition extends to both men and women, highlighting that polytheists invite to the Fire due to their deviation from Tawhid, whereas Allah invites to Paradise through divine guidance. This underscores the practical implication that a believing slave, despite lower worldly status, is superior to a free polytheist because their core belief aligns with the path to salvation.
